description:
ONE-TIME MANUAL STEP — performed by the human contributor (Chad / thewoolleyman)
via the GitHub UI + `gh secret set` CLI. Claude cannot perform App installation
on behalf of the user.

BACKGROUND
==========
The `livespec` GitHub App already exists and is installed on the `livespec`
repo (used by `auto-enable-merge.yml` and `auto-update-branches.yml`). It
has APP_ID + APP_PRIVATE_KEY secrets already configured at that repo level.

The cross-repo coordination automation surface requires the same App to be
installed on the other 3 sibling repos as well, with secrets propagated.

CURRENT STATE (verified as of session close)
============================================
Secrets per repo:
  - livespec:                 APP_ID + APP_PRIVATE_KEY present (from prior install)
  - livespec-dev-tooling:     NO secrets — needs install + secret set
  - livespec-runtime:         NO secrets — needs install + secret set
  - livespec-impl-plaintext:  NO secrets — needs install + secret set

GitHub topic livespec-sibling: present on all 4 repos (verified via Phase 4a).

Shim workflows: merged into all 4 repos pinned at livespec-dev-tooling@master:
  - livespec PR #224 (merged 2026-05-25T01:04:15Z)
  - livespec-dev-tooling PR #8 (merged 2026-05-25T01:05:13Z)
  - livespec-runtime PR #5 (merged 2026-05-25T01:04:46Z)
  - livespec-impl-plaintext PR #21 (merged 2026-05-25T01:04:49Z)

livespec-dev-tooling release v0.2.0 was cut (release-please PR #7 merged
2026-05-25T01:06:43Z); the reusable workflows are now consumable via
`livespec-dev-tooling/.github/workflows/reusable-*.yml@v0.2.0`.

STEP-BY-STEP INSTRUCTIONS
=========================

1. Navigate to the existing livespec GitHub App's settings page. The App
   is the one whose installation backs `auto-enable-merge.yml` in the
   livespec repo. Find it via either:

   a. GitHub UI: profile menu > Settings > Developer settings > GitHub Apps,
      look for the App that has the livespec scope.

   b. Or via the App's installation page on the livespec repo:
      https://github.com/thewoolleyman/livespec/settings/installations

2. From the App's settings page, verify it carries the following
   repository-level permissions (REQUIRED for the coordination surface
   per livespec-dev-tooling SPECIFICATION/contracts.md §"GitHub App auth model"):

     - contents: write       (to commit pin bumps + create branches)
     - pull-requests: write  (to open bump-pin PRs)
     - metadata: read        (for sibling discovery via topic query)

   If any of these are missing, edit the App's permissions to add them.
   GitHub will require existing installations to accept the new permissions
   on next use; this is a one-time prompt per installation.

3. Install the App on the 3 missing sibling repos:

     - thewoolleyman/livespec-dev-tooling
     - thewoolleyman/livespec-runtime
     - thewoolleyman/livespec-impl-plaintext

   From the App's installations page, click "Install" (or "Configure" if
   already partially installed), select the user thewoolleyman, then
   under "Repository access" choose "Only select repositories" and add
   the 3 repos above. Click Save.

4. Retrieve APP_ID and a fresh APP_PRIVATE_KEY:

     - APP_ID is shown on the App's "About" page. Note it down.

     - APP_PRIVATE_KEY: from the App's "Private keys" section, click
       "Generate a private key". A `.pem` file downloads. Copy its
       full contents (including the
       `-----BEGIN/END RSA PRIVATE KEY-----` lines).

5. Set the secrets on each of the 3 sibling repos via `gh secret set`:

     # Verify gh is authenticated with the right account
     gh auth status

     # Set APP_ID (same value across all 3 repos)
     echo "<APP_ID>" | gh secret set APP_ID -R thewoolleyman/livespec-dev-tooling
     echo "<APP_ID>" | gh secret set APP_ID -R thewoolleyman/livespec-runtime
     echo "<APP_ID>" | gh secret set APP_ID -R thewoolleyman/livespec-impl-plaintext

     # Set APP_PRIVATE_KEY (paste the full PEM content via stdin)
     gh secret set APP_PRIVATE_KEY -R thewoolleyman/livespec-dev-tooling < /path/to/private-key.pem
     gh secret set APP_PRIVATE_KEY -R thewoolleyman/livespec-runtime < /path/to/private-key.pem
     gh secret set APP_PRIVATE_KEY -R thewoolleyman/livespec-impl-plaintext < /path/to/private-key.pem

     # Verify each repo now has both secrets
     for r in livespec-dev-tooling livespec-runtime livespec-impl-plaintext; do
       echo "-- $r --"
       gh secret list -R thewoolleyman/$r
     done

6. After all 3 repos show APP_ID + APP_PRIVATE_KEY, this work-item is
   complete. The unblocks Phase 5b (smoke-test).

NEXT STEPS (Phase 5b, separate work-item li-tal73i)
===================================================
With the secrets in place, the smoke-test is:

  - Manually trigger pin-freshness on one sibling (Actions tab >
    "Pin freshness sweep" > Run workflow on master), OR
  - Tag a no-op patch release (e.g., livespec-runtime v0.2.1 from a
    chore:-only commit) and observe the release-dispatch fan-out.

Expected outcome:
  - dispatch fires from the source sibling
  - bump-pin PRs auto-open in the dependent siblings (via the App token)
  - CI passes
  - auto-merge lands the PRs

Document the verification trace in the work-item's closure narration.
title: Bootstrap GitHub App for cross-repo dispatch + record secrets

description:
OBSERVED 2026-05-25 during Phase 5b smoke-test and the post-epic convergence round: every bump-PR opened by the cross-repo coordination automation surface (reusable-bump-pin-from-dispatch.yml and reusable-pin-freshness.yml, both inline the `gh pr merge "$BRANCH" --auto --squash` step) hits an error that the workflow tolerates with `|| echo "::warning::could not enable auto-merge ..."`. Result: the PRs open cleanly with all CI passing, but `autoMergeRequest` stays null. PR #230 (livespec dev-tooling bump v0.1.1→v0.2.0) was the one positive case in the session — it auto-merged 20s after opening. PRs #22, #23, #235 all required manual `gh pr merge ... --squash` to land.

HYPOTHESIS:
  (a) `gh pr merge --auto` requires the auto-merge feature enabled       at the repo level (Settings > General > Pull Requests >       Allow auto-merge). PR #230 happened to be on livespec which       has it on; the 3 missing-secret repos may not have it on yet.
  (b) Branch-protection rules interact with App-token-authored       PRs differently than expected.
  (c) The App-token mint flow may need a different scope for the       `enablePullRequestAutoMerge` GraphQL mutation than what the       coordination App currently has.

INVESTIGATION PLAN:
  1. Check `Allow auto-merge` setting on each of the 4 sibling      repos. Enable if missing.
  2. Re-trigger pin-freshness on one repo and inspect the workflow      log for the actual `gh pr merge --auto` stderr (the current      workflow swallows it under `|| echo warning`).
  3. If still failing, check the livespec-pr-bot App's installation      permissions — `enablePullRequestAutoMerge` requires admin      repository access at the GraphQL layer.

PROPOSED FIX:
  Once root-caused, either: (i) enable the repo-level auto-merge   setting + add a workflow precondition checking it; or (ii)   rewrite the merge step to capture and surface stderr non-soft   so the failure is visible in the workflow run summary.

RELATED:
  - reusable-bump-pin-from-dispatch.yml step "Open auto-merge PR"
  - reusable-pin-freshness.yml step "Open auto-merge PR"
  - Cross-repo coordination epic li-7z7gqj (Phase 5b smoke-test)
title: `gh pr merge --auto` fails soft in bump-pin workflows; PRs land via manual merge or daily cron

description:
OBSERVED 2026-05-25 during the post-epic convergence round: merging release-please PR #6 on livespec-runtime created the v0.3.0 release at 16:20:11Z, but no `release-dispatch` workflow run was triggered (verified via `gh run list` and `gh api ... | jq '.workflow_runs[] | select(.event == "release")'` — zero release events on the runtime repo).

ROOT CAUSE: release-please uses `GITHUB_TOKEN` to publish the release, and GitHub does NOT fire `release` events for releases created by github-actions[bot]. This is the same workflow-recursion ceiling that motivated the App-token approach for `auto-enable-merge.yml` in livespec (commit a4073c7).

WORKAROUND USED THIS SESSION: manually triggered pin-freshness on the 3 consumer siblings, which discovered the stale livespec-runtime pin and opened bump PRs. Same end result via the cron safety-net path instead of the release-dispatch path.

REAL FIX:
  Rewire each sibling repo's release-please.yml to use the   livespec-pr-bot GitHub App token (via `actions/create-github-  app-token@v1`) instead of `GITHUB_TOKEN`. This is the standard   pattern documented at:
    https://github.com/googleapis/release-please-action#authenticating
    > 'If you wish to use a custom GitHub App, pass in the token     >  via the `token` input. Releases created via a GitHub App     >  token DO fire the release event, unblocking downstream     >  workflows.'

  This is a per-repo workflow rewire across all 4 sibling repos   (livespec, livespec-dev-tooling, livespec-runtime, livespec-impl-  plaintext) plus a contracts.md amendment in livespec-dev-tooling   to document the App-token-for-release-please convention as part   of the cross-repo coordination automation surface.

PROPOSE-CHANGE SCOPE (when ready):
  - Add §"release-please App-token convention" to dev-tooling     contracts.md §"Cross-repo coordination automation surface"
  - 4 follow-up PRs (one per sibling) rewriting release-please.yml
  - Add a check-CI-alignment invariant verifying release-please.yml     uses the App token (so future repos can't accidentally drift)

VERIFICATION (once fixed):
  Tag a no-op patch release in one sibling and confirm release-  dispatch.yml fires + bump PRs auto-open in dependent siblings.
title: release-please-created releases don't fire `release` event; release-dispatch.yml shims never trigger

description:
REFACTOR. Pre-flagged in the header of reusable-pin-freshness.yml §"Sub-workflow choice". The pin-rewrite logic — clone consumer, run autodiscovery for a specific source, edit matching pins to a new tag, optionally re-vendor, run `just check`, commit with the chore(deps): prefix, push, open auto-merge PR — is duplicated across:
  - reusable-bump-pin-from-dispatch.yml (called from     release-dispatch -> repository_dispatch)
  - reusable-pin-freshness.yml (called from cron-triggered     pin-autodiscovery)

WHY THE DUPLICATION HAPPENED:
  Reusable workflows can only be invoked at job level (not step   level), so pin-freshness can't call bump-pin-from-dispatch as a   sub-workflow without dynamic per-source job creation. The   duplication is the YAGNI shape for v1.

CONSOLIDATION OPTIONS:
  (a) Extract the rewrite step body into a composite Action at       `.github/actions/bump-pin-rewrite/action.yml`. Both reusable       workflows call the Action via `uses: ./.github/actions/...`.       This is the cleanest fix — composite Actions ARE step-level       invokable.
  (b) Bash-script the rewrite body, dump to `.github/scripts/bump-      pin-rewrite.sh`, call from both workflows. Works but loses       the typed-input contract a composite Action provides.

WHEN TO FIX:
  Only when the duplication becomes painful to maintain (e.g., a   bug fix in one workflow has to be remembered in the other).   Currently both workflows are stable and the divergence risk is   low. Priority 3 (low) for backlog.

ESTIMATED EFFORT: ~half a day for option (a), TDD-driven via the fixture-based pin-autodiscovery test suite plus a smoke test that both workflows invoke the new composite Action.

RELATED:
  - .github/workflows/reusable-bump-pin-from-dispatch.yml
  - .github/workflows/reusable-pin-freshness.yml
  - Cross-repo coordination epic li-7z7gqj (Phase 3)
title: Pin-rewrite step body duplicated between bump-pin-from-dispatch and pin-freshness workflows

description:
FEATURE. The shim workflows in each sibling repo (release-dispatch.yml, bump-pin-from-dispatch.yml, pin-freshness.yml) pin livespec-dev-tooling@master as the bootstrap discipline. The cross-repo coordination contract says: 'the first sibling release post-this-PR triggers a bump-pin PR rewriting @master to a tag.'

BUT: the current pin_autodiscovery.py only walks 4 formats: .livespec.jsonc compat.pinned, pyproject.toml [tool.uv.sources], .vendor.jsonc, .copier-answers.yml _commit. Workflow `uses:` references are NOT in scope. So the @master pins in the shim workflows stay @master forever unless either (a) someone manually rewrites them, or (b) autodiscovery is extended.

PROPOSED EXTENSION:
  Add a 5th pin format: `github_workflow_uses_ref`. The walker   parses every YAML file under .github/workflows/ and emits a   record per matching `uses: <owner>/<repo>/...@<ref>` line   where the repo has the livespec-sibling topic (or matches a   configurable allowlist). The pin's source_repo is derived from   the `<repo>` segment; current_value is `<ref>`.

  Rewrite path: when bump-pin runs, sed-replace the `@<ref>`   with the new tag in every matched file.

PROPOSE-CHANGE SCOPE (when ready):
  - Extend dev-tooling contracts.md §"Pin autodiscovery rules"     to enumerate the new format.
  - Extend dev-tooling constraints.md §"Semver discipline" to     cover the new format's surface (adding workflow-ref scanning     is a MINOR bump per the existing semver discipline).
  - Implement the new format in pin_autodiscovery.py with paired     tests under tests/livespec_dev_tooling/cross_repo/.
  - The bump-pin workflows already use a generic per-format-    rewrite step body — they should handle the new format with     a small case-block extension.

VERIFICATION (once landed):
  Trigger pin-freshness on any sibling whose shim workflows pin   @master. Expect a bump PR rewriting @master to @v0.2.0 (or   whatever the current dev-tooling release is).

RELATED:
  - livespec_dev_tooling/cross_repo/pin_autodiscovery.py
  - .github/workflows/reusable-bump-pin-from-dispatch.yml (the     'Rewrite matching pins to new tag' step)
  - Cross-repo coordination epic li-7z7gqj (Phase 4 shim drops)
title: Extend pin-autodiscovery to walk `.github/workflows/*.yml` for `uses: <sibling>/...@<ref>` lines

description:
Cross-repo follow-up from livespec's /livespec:revise v081 (PC #2: coordinating-epic-stale-revise-enforcement, Sub-proposal 2 / Layer 1). This is the child PC's underlying mechanism — the shared git-topology check that the parent PC's `skills/revise/SKILL.md` Step 3.5 (filed in livespec's queue) will invoke pre-revise.

Scope:
- Implement a new shared check module `no_stale_revise_branches` in   livespec-dev-tooling's check surface (location per dev-tooling's own   contracts.md; check the §"Cross-repo coordination automation surface"   or wherever shared checks live).
- The check:
  - Enumerates local refs matching refs/heads/spec/* via
    `git for-each-ref --format='%(refname:short)' refs/heads/spec/`.
  - For each, computes ahead-count vs origin/<canonical_branch> via
    `git rev-list --left-right --count <branch>...origin/<canonical>`.
  - Returns `fail` findings for every branch ahead by one or more commits.
- The canonical_branch lookup defaults to `master`; consumer projects   with a non-master default branch supply it via the runtime config.
- Add unit tests + fixture git repos.
- The check is shipped from livespec-dev-tooling and CONSUMED by
  livespec's revise SKILL.md Step 3.5; the integration test for that
  Step 3.5 wraps this check.

Per the parent PC body: this is the child PC `no-stale-revise-branches-check`.
title: Implement no_stale_revise_branches shared check (Layer 1 underlying mechanism)
